A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey. Their complete text, tables, figures and appendices support comparison. The case-study table from v2 Appendix D is retained in v3 Section 6, rather than deleted.

before.justification: v2 reports literature summaries and descriptive case studies of Llama-3 and INTELLECT-1. Numerical outcomes are attributed to cited work; neither the main text nor appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: v3 remains a literature survey without original empirical results. Its additional GPT-3 memory comparison and INTELLECT-2 discussion concern cited work, and its multimodal and reinforcement-learning proposals are future directions.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes a training algorithm or model. Replacing expert parallelism with context parallelism in Appendix A changes the survey's explanatory coverage, not a proposed method.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or evaluation on datasets. Multimodal training and reinforcement-learning post-training receive new discussion, but no datasets or test scenarios are actually evaluated by this work.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates baselines against a proposed method. Tables 1 and 2 retain their survey and system memberships. The Switch Transformer-to-DeepSpeed-Ulysses substitution in Appendix A concerns illustrative frameworks, not experimentally evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: No experimental protocol is introduced or revised. The retained case studies report the same model sizes, hardware scales and training durations. The token-unit correction in the relocated configuration table does not establish a changed training setting; v2 Section 6 already described Llama-3's 15 T tokens.

E4.justification: The same two descriptive case studies are retained, with no added ablations, robustness tests or developed case analysis. The brief INTELLECT-2 mention supplies literature context rather than a new analysis; moving the configuration table changes presentation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Changing Llama-3's effective training time from 90% to ≥90% does not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Llama-3's reported effective training time changes from 90% in v2 Table 4 to ≥90% in v3 Table 3. Section 2.4 also newly quotes GPT-3 activation memory exceeding parameter memory by more than 5×. These are changes to reported literature findings, not demonstrated performance gains from new experiments.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal mathematical results or proofs. The revised scaling-law passage is an informal hypothesis, and the parallelism descriptions remain conceptual rather than mathematical definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and summary retain the same central contributions: a resource-driven survey, the community-driven versus organizational taxonomy, optimization-oriented literature synthesis, and illustrative case studies. The expanded research agenda does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 2.4 adds an activation-memory rationale for sophisticated parallelism. Section 7.2 replaces an upper-bound-on-model-size hypothesis with a practical scaling-efficiency limit and adds modality-specific scheduling and RL rollout/backward coordination challenges. The earlier explicit limitation concerning reasoning and vision-language models is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix A expands technical descriptions of communication primitives and activation-memory partitioning, including context parallelism and DeepSpeed-Ulysses. The case-study table clarifies token entries from '15 TB / 1 TB' to '15 T / 1 T'. Hardware configurations and training durations are retained; no new reproducibility artifacts or access instructions appear.

R1.justification: v3 adds literature on INTELLECT-2, DistMM, vLLM/SGLang, FSDP, DeepSpeed-Ulysses and recent compression/delay methods, while removing the Switch Transformers reference. Section 6 also drops INTELLECT-1's attributed 'first' claim. The survey's overall positioning against prior surveys remains stable.

P1.justification: Localized revisions expand Sections 2.4 and 7.2, rewrite case-study and Appendix A prose, update affiliations and add acknowledgments. The principal section sequence and most literature-review prose remain intact; Appendix D's content is incorporated into Section 6.

P2.justification: The organizational taxonomy moves from v2 Figure 3 in Appendix B to v3 Figure 2 in Section 5, and the case-study table moves into Section 6. The parallelism table replaces its expert-parallelism column with context parallelism, removes the computation-concurrency row and revises labels. Figure 1 receives small label and layout edits.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the survey more useful through the clearer parallelism rationale in Section 2.4, a more qualified scaling hypothesis, and concrete multimodal and RL coordination challenges in Section 7.2. Moving case configurations beside their discussion and correcting token units improve usability and consistency. Appendix A gains context-parallelism detail while losing its expert-parallelism comparison, limiting the net improvement within an otherwise largely retained survey.
